name: ACE Product Filters – AJAX Filters for WooCommerce
author: Stefano Papa | Ace Plugins

sections.description:
ACE Product Filters started after years of testing other WooCommerce filter plugins, including paid options, and still not finding one that handled the full workflow cleanly. It began as a filter system built to cover real storefront needs end to end, and once it proved reliable, it was shared so other store owners and builders could use the same approach.

ACE Product Filters gives you a practical way to build WooCommerce filters once and reuse them across your storefront.

Create saved filter sets for categories, global attributes, product taxonomies, and price ranges, style them to match your store, and place them individually or inside reusable filter panels. Whether you are building a shop sidebar, a top bar, or a custom Elementor layout, you can keep the filtering experience consistent without rebuilding the same setup for every page.

🆓 The free plugin already includes:

  • Unlimited saved category, attribute, product taxonomy, and price filter sets
  • Saved filter panels for sidebars, top bars, and grouped storefront layouts
  • AJAX filtering with a shared results selector, URL filter state, and browser history
  • Price range filtering with optional Min / Max inputs
  • Support for product tags, brands, manufacturers, and other registered product taxonomies
  • Single-select and multi-select, with optional AND or OR matching
  • Auto-include child terms when a parent is selected, plus optional nested term indentation
  • Changeable shortcode IDs for saved filter sets and filter panels
  • Product counts and labels, with static or contextual count modes and optional panel-wide overrides
  • Hide terms with no matching products, per filter or as a panel override
  • In-filter term search for long lists, with a search box option and a panel override
  • Colour swatches for any taxonomy filter, with square or circle chips, spread or column layout, a hex colour per term, and an optional background behind the chips
  • Panel headings, grouped heading blocks inside panels, and collapsible filters
  • Empty-results messaging
  • Horizontal or vertical layout, plus styling controls for filters and panels, including responsive and mobile presentation
  • Live appearance preview in the filter editor
  • Theme-font inheritance by default, with optional Google Fonts loading when you explicitly enable it
  • Mobile panel toggle, close button, and per-panel text for the Filters label and Clear all action
  • Elementor widget support plus shortcode placement
  • Reusable output for shop pages, category archives, Elementor templates, and custom storefront sections

Use one saved filter when you need a focused control, or combine multiple saved filters into a panel for a complete storefront filtering experience.

📍 Placement options:

  • Elementor widget for saved filters and saved panels
  • Shortcode for practical use with Wonderblocks or other website builders
  • Block editor, widgets, and theme template areas

Usage

  1. Create a filter set and choose whether it should use categories, attributes, product taxonomies, or price.
  2. Configure the behavior, labels, counts, layout direction, and design settings.
  3. Enable AJAX when you want in-place product updates and set one shared results selector.
  4. Place the saved filter directly, or create a filter panel and combine multiple saved filters into one reusable block.
  5. Insert the result through the Elementor widget or shortcode wherever your storefront layout needs it.

External services

ACE Product Filters can optionally load Google Fonts stylesheets only when a site owner enables Google Fonts loading in the plugin settings and uses Google Font families in filter designs or live preview.

By default, ACE Product Filters does not request Google Fonts on the frontend or in the plugin admin.

These requests can happen on ACE Product Filters admin pages and on frontend pages where ACE Product Filters output is rendered.

Service provider:

  • Google Fonts API: https://fonts.googleapis.com/
  • Google Fonts static files: https://fonts.gstatic.com/

What may be sent:

  • The site visitor or admin user’s IP address
  • Browser and device information
  • The requesting site URL through normal HTTP request metadata

Service terms and policies:

  • Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Terms of Service: https://policies.google.com/terms
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the zip from the WordPress admin.
  2. Activate ACE Product Filters.
  3. Make sure WooCommerce is active.
  4. Go to ACE Product Filters in the WordPress admin.
  5. Create your first filter set, then optionally group filters into a panel.
  6. Place the saved filter or panel with the Elementor widget, the block editor, a shortcode widget, or a template area.
sections.faq:
Is the free version actually powerful enough to use on its own?

Yes. The free plugin already includes unlimited saved category, attribute, product taxonomy, and price filters, saved filter panels, AJAX updates, styling controls, mobile panel settings, and Elementor support.

Does it work only with Elementor?

No. Elementor is supported through a dedicated widget, and the plugin also works with shortcodes in regular WordPress pages, widgets, and template areas.

Does it support AJAX filtering?

Yes. Enable AJAX and enter one stable CSS selector for the shared results wrapper.

Can I combine multiple saved filters together?

Yes. Create saved filter sets individually, then group them into saved filter panels for sidebars, top bars, or multi-filter layouts.

Can I use it with product category archives?

Yes. It is designed for WooCommerce archive filtering and can also be placed on custom pages.

Does uninstall delete my saved filters?

No. At the moment, deleting the plugin does not automatically remove saved filter sets, filter panels, or related display settings from the database.
sections.changelog:
1.2.2

• New: You can now hide terms with no matching products, per filter set, with a panel override (inherit / hide / show).
• New: In-filter term search for long lists, with terms-only or search box and terms, customizable placeholder and search-box styles, and a panel override.
• New: Colour swatches for taxonomy filters, with square or circle chips, spread or column layout, a hex colour per term, and an optional background behind the chips.

1.2.1

• Verified compatibility with WordPress 7.1.
• Per-filter match logic: multi-select filters can now require products to match all selected terms (AND) instead of any one term (OR).
• Parent category select-all: when a parent term is checked in a multi-select filter, its child terms from the same filter set are automatically selected.
• New: Grouped filter headings: add, remove, and drag heading blocks inside a panel to group the filters below them. Headings can be styled from the panel appearance settings.
• Improved: Optional nested term indentation: hierarchical filters can show child terms indented under their parents, or stay in a flat custom-order list.
• Other minor improvements.

1.2

• New: Added per-filter count display modes plus an optional panel-wide override so grouped filters can stay aligned without editing each set one by one.
• New: Added per-panel custom text fields for the mobile Filters label and the Clear all action.
• New: Added changeable shortcode IDs for saved filter sets and filter panels, with safe auto-generated fallbacks when needed.
• Improved: Fixed the filter-set preview refresh so styling changes can be updated reliably from the editor without saving the filter first.
• Improved: Completed a full UX overhaul of the dashboard plus the filter set and filter panel editors for a cleaner, more manageable workflow.

1.1.2

• Fixed an issue where the Show Count setting could not be properly disabled.
• Fixed incorrect contextual product counts when using multiple filter sets.
• Fixed count values bleeding between filter sets during AJAX filtering.
• Improved filtering logic to correctly preserve filter-set boundaries, including when multiple sets use the same taxonomy.
• Improved saving and persistence of Show Label, Show Count, and AJAX settings.
• Improved contextual count recalculation when multiple filters are active.
• Refreshed and polished the admin interface with improved colors, spacing, and visual consistency.
• Updated plugin branding from Ace Products Filters to ACE Product Filters.
• General stability and usability improvements.

1.1.1

• New: Added a global setting to enable or disable Google Fonts loading.
• Improved: Google Fonts are now disabled by default.
• Improved: When no font is selected, the plugin now correctly inherits your theme’s typography instead of loading default fonts.
• Improved: The admin preview now respects the Google Fonts setting.
• Improved: Updated font settings descriptions for better clarity.

1.1.0

Added product taxonomy filter support for WooCommerce catalogs.

1.0.2

Verified compatibility with WordPress 7.0.

1.0.1

Fixed mobile filter-set and panel collapse behavior so closed states work correctly on small screens.

1.0.0

Initial stable release of ACE Product Filters with AJAX filtering, filter panels, price filters, Elementor-friendly selectors, configurable empty states, and improved contextual count performance.
